It now reads 'Gusu', the conventional name of the Wu capital site at modern Suzhou; `name_en` is the conventional English name, not the strictly attested one (conventions §1). WHAT THE BASIS IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT — stated because it is thinner than the rename looks, and because nothing here should be read as a claim the sources do not make. The classical corpus gives the Wu capital no proper name at all: chunqiu's exhaustive string check of the whole Zuozhuan (its docs/kaoding_wudu.md at the pin 6beb833294fa535b874e3d640fa80fa7101cfce1, cited not quoted — that file is outside the DATA_LICENSE scope — read this session, read-only per D-18) returns zero hits for 姑苏 and 姑胥 and for every other candidate town name, and records that the Chunqiu classic, the Zuozhuan and the Guoyu write the state name 吳 wherever the capital is meant, as they do for Qi, Lu, Zheng, Chen and Cai. The earliest uses of 姑蘇 name a terrace and a palace at the site rather than the town, and the one that is inside chunqiu's own CC BY 4.0 tables — read at the pin this session, in data/csv/event_people.csv row E253 and data/csv/passages.csv row Q408, and cited here in the script those rows print — is 《国语·越语下》「至於姑蘇之宮」 with Wei Zhao's gloss on 《国语·吴语》 「王臺，姑蘇」, the royal terrace the Yue army surrounded when it entered the Wu capital. So 'Gusu' is the conventional name of the place, not a name the Spring-and-Autumn sources give the town; and which place it is remains disputed four ways, which is why this row's `coord_certainty` is low (see `coord_basis`). `name_original` is left as found (吳) — see data/incoming/round06/CHANGES.md §6 for the script question put to the lead.
